LVKE.|183}}</noinclude>found it, laieth it vpon his {{ls}}houlders reioycing: {{verse|chapter=15|verse=6}} and comming home calleth together his frendes and neighbours, {{ls}}aying to them, Reioyce vvith me, becau{{ls}}e I haue found my {{ls}}heepe that vvas lo{{ls}}t? {{verse|chapter=15|verse=7}} I {{ls}}ay to you, that euen {{ls}}o there {{ls}}hal be ioy in heauen vpon one {{ls}}inner that doth penance, {{sup|‖}} then vpon ninetie nine iu{{ls}}t that neede not penance. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=8}} Or vvhat {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ This woman is the catholike Church, vvho al{{ls}}o continually {{ls}}eeketh her lo{{ls}}t children.}}∷ vvoman hauing ten grotes: if {{ls}}he lee{{ls}}e one grote, doth {{ls}}he not light a candle, and {{ls}}weepe the hou{{ls}}e, and {{ls}}eeke diligently, vntil {{ls}}he finde? {{verse|chapter=15|verse=9}} And vvhen {{ls}}he hath found, calleth together her frendes and neighbours, {{ls}}aying, Reioyce vvith me, becau{{ls}}e I haue found the grote vvhich I had lo{{ls}}t? {{verse|chapter=15|verse=10}} So, I {{ls}}ay to you, there {{ls}}hal be ioy {{sup|‖}} before the Angels of God vpon one {{ls}}inner that doth penance.⊣

{{verse|chapter=15|verse=11}} {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Go{{ls}}pel vpō Saturday in the 2 weeke of Lent.}}And he {{ls}}aid, A certaine man had tvvo {{ls}}onnes: {{verse|chapter=15|verse=12}} and the yonger of them {{ls}}aid to his father, Father, giue me the portion of {{ls}}ub{{ls}}tance that belongeth to me. And he deuided vnto them the {{ls}}ub{{ls}}tance. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=13}} {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The prodigal {{ls}}onne, is a parable, both of the Gentils conuer{{ls}}ion, & al{{ls}}o of euery di{{ls}}{{ls}}olute {{ls}}inner penitently returning to God.}}∷ And not many daies after the yonger {{ls}}onne gathering al his things together vvent from home into a farre countrie: and there he wa{{ls}}ted his {{ls}}ub{{ls}}tance, liuing riotou{{ls}}ly. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=14}} And after he had {{ls}}pent al, there fel a {{ls}}ore famine in that countrie, and he began to be in neede. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=15}} And he vvent, and cleaued to one of the citizens of that countrie. And he {{ls}}ent him into his farme to feede {{ls}}vvine. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=16}} And he vvould faine haue filled his bellie of the hu{{ls}}kes that the {{ls}}vvine did eate: and no bodie gaue vnto him. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=17}} And returning to him {{ls}}elf he {{ls}}aid, Hovv many of my fathers hirelings haue aboundance of bread: and I here peri{{ls}}h for famine? {{verse|chapter=15|verse=18}} I vvil ari{{ls}}e, and vvil goe to my father, and {{ls}}ay to him, Father, I haue {{ls}}inned again{{ls}}t heauen and before thee: {{verse|chapter=15|verse=19}} I am not novv vvorthie to be called thy {{ls}}onne: make me as one of thy hirelings. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=20}} And ri{{ls}}ing vp he came to his father. And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Gods wonderful and tender mercie toward penitent {{ls}}inners.}}∷ vvhen he vvas yet farre of, his father {{ls}}avv him, and vvas moued vvith mercie, and running to him fel vpon his necke, and ki{{ls}}sed him. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=21}} And his {{ls}}onne {{ls}}aid to him, Father, I haue {{ls}}inned again{{ls}}t heauen & before thee, I am not novv vvorthie to be called thy {{ls}}onne. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=22}} And the father {{ls}}aid to his {{ls}}eruants, Quickely bring forth the fir{{ls}}t {{ls}}tole, and doe it on him, and put a ring vpon his hand, and {{ls}}hoes vpon his feete: {{verse|chapter=15|verse=23}} and bring {{sup|‖}} the fatted calfe, and kil it, and let vs eate, and make merie: {{verse|chapter=15|verse=24}} becau{{ls}}e this my {{ls}}onne vvas dead, and is reuiued: vvas lo{{ls}}t, and is found. And they began to make merie. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=25}} But his elder {{ls}}onne vvas in the field.<noinclude>{{rh|||and}}</noinclude>
